Category: Object.
Subject: piano accordion.
Style: Italian mother-of-pearl.
reasoning:
I'm planning the accordion as a static model with realistic proportions—roughly half a meter wide, tall, and deep—and deciding how to orient it upright with the piano keys facing forward.

I'll just assign concrete dimensions: treble case roughly 0.17 wide along x, with a keyboard face on +Z holding 34 keys stacked along the case height, each about 0.01 tall, sized and oriented to protrude outward as small key boxes.

For the finish, I'm going with a mother-of-pearl look -- a pearly, iridescent white body for the case.

Now I'm working out the color scheme and component layout: deep wine-red bellows with gold trim against the pearl-white case, plus black ornamental details and a chrome grille. I'm sketching out the positioning of the treble case, bass case, and bellows along the x-axis, with the overall height and depth dimensions for the standing figure.

For the bellows pleats, I'm figuring out how to build the zigzag fold pattern using an extruded outline approach rather than many individual boxes, working through the geometry of alternating thin and thick plates to get a convincing accordion-fold look.

Adjusting the zigzag amplitudes...

Adding thin gold rods at the bellows corners, then sketching the bass case as a pearl-colored box at the -X end, with the button grid placed on the +Z face for visibility.

For the treble side, I'm working out the keyboard proportions: picking 21 white keys at roughly 0.0175 spacing to span the 0.40 height, with 15 black keys interspersed in the standard pattern, mirroring the bass buttons on the same +Z face for a consistent frontal view.

Now I'm placing keys as separate parts protruding slightly from the keyboard face—white keys raised a bit, black keys raised higher—merging white and black key geometries separately by color while keeping part counts manageable. For the bass side I'm laying out the button grid, considering 6 columns by 9 rows of small cylindrical buttons on the case front.

Then I'm detailing decorative end plates: a chrome fretwork grille on the treble case's outer face, an ornate emblem on the bass end, register switch rectangles on the treble top, and a logo plate near the front. I'm also defining a pearl nacre paint function that blends pearl white with pink and aqua tones using layered noise to create a mottled, iridescent surface.

Now I'm thinking through black celluloid binding along the case edges — thin protruding strips at the top and bottom edges of each case — plus gold trim rods, and I'm sketching out a gold floral/curve grille pattern on a dark background for the decorative plates.

Still writing SVG code...

For the bellows I'm shading them red with pearl-white textile pleats using a periodic function along x to create ridge-and-valley coloring, mixing dark and bright tones based on a zigzag pattern, with pearl edging where the pleats meet the end plates.

Now I'm defining the extruded outline for the bellows geometry, placing zigzag points along x with alternating z depths for front and back, mirrored and marked sharp, centered at y=0.2 with a thickness of 0.37 so front and back don't self-intersect. I'm starting on the second outline for the top pleats, this time varying y instead of z, keeping it centered around 0.2 as well.

Working out the treble case dimensions and deciding to keep it as simple boxes rather than adding curved shaping, then moving on to positioning the keyboard keys along the front face centered on x.

For spacing, I'm computing 21 white key positions evenly along y, then figuring out which keys get black keys between them following the standard C-D-E-F-G-A-B pattern (skipping after E and B), and placing those black keys shorter and offset toward one end of the white keys.

Checking key depths line up correctly, then I need to widen the treble case slightly so the keybed fits with proper margins on all sides, and figure out where the end caps attach.

Placing the X-axis end plates for treble and bass sides, orienting them to face outward with the correct texture dimensions, then positioning the bass-side button plate within its case bounds.

Now I'm laying out the button grid for the bass case front: 6 columns by 9 rows of pearl-topped cylinder buttons with gold rings, merging their geometries into a single mesh with proper rotation so the cylinders face outward, and marking a subset of them as darker root-marker buttons for visual distinction.

For the top edges, I'm adding a thin black back strap with a gold buckle on the bass side, a black register-switch panel with small pearl tabs on the treble top, and a small gold air-release button with a pearl cap near the bass case top.

Now I'm adding decorative banding along the case edges: black binding strips wrapping the top and bottom fronts of each case, with thin gold accent lines running just inside them, plus gold corner caps for a finished look.

I'm positioning small gold rods at the bellows corners to act as decorative rail protectors, nestled into the pleat ridges so they stay mostly embedded but still catch the light. Now I'm moving on to the texture SVGs, starting with the treble end piece—a rounded black rectangle with a gold border and a central pearl medallion.

Still writing the rosette...

Next I sketch the bass end with a similar frame but swap the rosette for an eight-point star plus "MILANO" text, then design a brand plate with a gold rectangle and italic "Fiorelli" serif lettering, and consider whether to add a pearl swirl inlay strip as an extra decorative touch.

Simplifying from there: I'll skip extra decals and fascia details, keep gold as a flat hex color instead of a textured paint, and leave the body without visible feet since it rests flat on the floor. I'm setting up a static part builder with helper functions for creating boxes and planes to assemble the instrument geometry.

Working out the brand plate positioning and pearl paint function...

Adding thin vein lines and a bellows paint function with a triangular ridge pattern shading from dark red to bright accent color...

Setting the strap to flat black leather, then building the gold rod helpers with flat-cap sweeps for the accordion frame. I'm also laying out the bass button grid in rows and columns with spacing offsets, and planning a pearl grille cap detail on the treble side plus decorative inlay above the bass buttons.

Now I'm working out vertical placement for the button plate, brand label, and top band, then adding a dark/light pattern to alternate buttons using a modulo rule. I'm positioning each button as a small rotated cylinder sitting just in front of the plate surface, calculating the exact z-depth so buttons sit flush against the plate face.

Finishing the ring and pearl button geometry, then moving on to writing out the SVG texture strings before assembling everything together.
